newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Russia presses case to enter WTO but road long.
newsitem.headline: Russia presses case to enter WTO but road long.

text.p: Russia pushed its case for gaining entry to the World Trade Organisation (WTO) on Tuesday, as some of its trading partners expressed concern about government control over import licensing schemes, trade officials said.
Assistant U.S. Trade Representative Dorothy Dwoskin was among those who raised the issue at the WTO working party negotiating Moscow's terms of entry to the 123-member watchdog.
"Some concern was expressed how the current import licensing registration works and whether it is compatible with WTO rules," a senior U.S. trade official told Reuters.
"The Russians have done a useful job in beginning to show where their non-tariff measures are. Some are WTO-compatible and some don't appear to be," the official added.
Russian officials had shown a constructive attitude in the session, the fourth since 1993, according to trade sources who said they still expected Moscow's road to membership to be long.

Other Russian non-tariff measures, including customs valuation, were examined during the first day on Tuesday. Its agricultural policies, including internal support and export subsidies, will be discussed informally on Wednesday.
"I would say we have turned a corner in the discussions. There is much more focus and detailed infromation. It wasn't just fact-finding," the senior U.S. trade official said.
Georgi Gabounia, deputy minister of foreign economic relations, is heading a 20-strong delegation from Moscow.
In an opening speech to trade delegates, Gabounia said Russia was focusing on achieving macroeconomic stability.
Exports jumped to 20 per cent of gross domestic product in 1995, against an average of seven per cent during the 1991-93 period, he said.
